# Finding the Antiderivative of $-x^5 \sin(3x)$

## Setting Up the Tabular Method

I'll use the **tabular integration by parts** method, differentiating $-x^5$ and integrating $\sin(3x)$ repeatedly.

| Sign | Differentiate ($-x^5$) | Integrate ($\sin(3x)$) |
|------|------------------------|------------------------|
| $+$ | $-x^5$ | $\sin(3x)$ |
| $-$ | $-5x^4$ | $-\frac{\cos(3x)}{3}$ |
| $+$ | $-20x^3$ | $-\frac{\sin(3x)}{9}$ |
| $-$ | $-60x^2$ | $\frac{\cos(3x)}{27}$ |
| $+$ | $-120x$ | $\frac{\sin(3x)}{81}$ |
| $-$ | $-120$ | $-\frac{\cos(3x)}{243}$ |
| $+$ | $0$ | $-\frac{\sin(3x)}{729}$ |

## Combining Terms

Each term is: **(sign) × (D column) × (I column below)**

| # | Sign | D value | I value | Result |
|---|------|---------|---------|--------|
| 1 | $+$ | $-x^5$ | $-\frac{\cos(3x)}{3}$ | $+\frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3}$ |
| 2 | $-$ | $-5x^4$ | $-\frac{\sin(3x)}{9}$ | $-\frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9}$ |
| 3 | $+$ | $-20x^3$ | $\frac{\cos(3x)}{27}$ | $-\frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27}$ |
| 4 | $-$ | $-60x^2$ | $\frac{\sin(3x)}{81}$ | $+\frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27}$ |
| 5 | $+$ | $-120x$ | $-\frac{\cos(3x)}{243}$ | $+\frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81}$ |
| 6 | $-$ | $-120$ | $-\frac{\sin(3x)}{729}$ | $-\frac{40\sin(3x)}{243}$ |

## Verification

Differentiating the result step by step, all intermediate terms cancel telescopically, leaving exactly $-x^5\sin(3x)$ ✓

## Final Answer

$$\frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3} - \frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9} - \frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27} + \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27} + \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81} - \frac{40\sin(3x)}{243} + C$$
